Theme: Older adults preserve agency inside collective medication work
Organizing concept: Older adults retain forms of action while knowledge, reminders, supply, and authority circulate through a care network.
Sub-theme: Taking and knowing are different forms of competence
What it means: Familiar packaging and routine can support taking without biomedical name recall.
Boundary and variation: Kin-held knowledge does not automatically replace older adult action.

Theme: Older adults preserve agency inside collective medication work
Organizing concept: Older adults retain forms of action while knowledge, reminders, supply, and authority circulate through a care network.
Sub-theme: Reminding circulates through relationships and presence
What it means: Spouses, children, and peers cue remembering within ordinary routines.
Boundary and variation: Circulation does not mean that no person carries primary responsibility.

Theme: Older adults preserve agency inside collective medication work
Organizing concept: Older adults retain forms of action while knowledge, reminders, supply, and authority circulate through a care network.
What it means: Some older adults manage with memory, notes, or prescriptions and reject current technology need.
Boundary and variation: Refusal remains a legitimate form of participation.

Theme: Routine transitions expose coordination problems, not a general memory deficit
Organizing concept: Breakdowns occur when time, place, people, supply, or packaging no longer align.
Sub-theme: Changed time and place displace familiar cues
What it means: Travel, visitors, work, and delayed meals interrupt otherwise workable routines.
Boundary and variation: Remembering the schedule does not ensure that medicine is present.

Theme: Routine transitions expose coordination problems, not a general memory deficit
Organizing concept: Breakdowns occur when time, place, people, supply, or packaging no longer align.
Sub-theme: Family availability shapes whether a lapse is noticed
What it means: Shared reminding can fail when everyone is busy or a caregiver is away.
Boundary and variation: Distance creates uncertainty rather than proof of a missed dose.

Theme: Routine transitions expose coordination problems, not a general memory deficit
Organizing concept: Breakdowns occur when time, place, people, supply, or packaging no longer align.
Sub-theme: Supply and packaging create non-reminder failures
What it means: A finished strip blocks action and a changed package can disrupt recognition.
Boundary and variation: These failures require more than reminder salience.

Theme: Current tools support fragments of practice and create new handoffs
Organizing concept: Alarms, papers, notes, locations, calls, and shared devices each support bounded tasks.
Sub-theme: Generic alarms attract attention without specifying action
What it means: An alarm may be noticed but not identify the medicine or produce immediate action.
Boundary and variation: One older adult finds alarms helpful despite deferral.

Theme: Current tools support fragments of practice and create new handoffs
Organizing concept: Alarms, papers, notes, locations, calls, and shared devices each support bounded tasks.
Sub-theme: Device and document access shape participation
What it means: Multi-step apps, button phones, small print, and handwriting alter who can act directly.
Boundary and variation: These are interaction conditions rather than age-based incapacity.

Theme: Current tools support fragments of practice and create new handoffs
Organizing concept: Alarms, papers, notes, locations, calls, and shared devices each support bounded tasks.
Sub-theme: Existing practices may already be sufficient
What it means: Notes, prescriptions, fixed locations, and family questions remain effective for some older adults.
Boundary and variation: Technology need cannot be inferred from age alone.

Theme: Future technology is acceptable when it extends the care network
Organizing concept: Older adults favor direct participation, selective family support, and continuing human authority.
Sub-theme: Voice and visual cues connect prompts to familiar medicines
What it means: Spoken Bangla, medicine names, pictures, and simple controls can reduce screen dependence.
Boundary and variation: One privacy countercase requires a quieter alternative.
RQ and contribution: RQ1 with formative support for RQ3; C3 basis

Theme: Future technology is acceptable when it extends the care network
Organizing concept: Older adults favor direct participation, selective family support, and continuing human authority.
Sub-theme: Escalation communicates exceptions rather than continuous compliance
What it means: A repeat and time to respond should precede family notification.
Boundary and variation: Digital confirmation remains subordinate to medicine taking.
RQ and contribution: RQ1 with formative support for RQ3; C3 basis

Theme: Future technology is acceptable when it extends the care network
Organizing concept: Older adults favor direct participation, selective family support, and continuing human authority.
Sub-theme: Trust remains attached to accountable people
What it means: Kin may configure and verify information while doctors retain medication authority.
Boundary and variation: Phase 1 does not show negotiated agent allegiance through use.
RQ and contribution: RQ1 with formative support for RQ3; C3 basis
